cadenas.propuesta_en: An LLC separates personal and business liability, which matters when you tow a smoker and cook with fire at other people's events. An S corp election can cut self-employment tax once profit is steady; ask your accountant when it pays off.

Apply on your state tax agency website. In many states sales tax applies to the whole catering invoice: smoked meats, staff and rentals, and in some states the service charge. Confirm your state's rule before you quote.

Bring the Word plan, the Excel projections and written quotes for the smoker trailer and the van. SBA 7(a) loans go through participating banks: ask what owner equity they expect and how long approval takes, and do not sign for the trailer until the loan is approved.
Have an attorney draft your standard BBQ catering contract

Cover a 50% nonrefundable deposit, final payment date, cancellation tiers, guest minimum, final guest count date, and service charge versus gratuity. Add a weather and burn ban clause (propane backup or a new date) and photo permission. Reuse it for every event.

cadenas.propuesta_en: Safe minimums (FDA Food Code): 145 °F (63 °C) for intact cuts, 155 °F (68 °C) for injected, tenderized or ground meat including sausage (an injected brisket counts), 165 °F (74 °C) for poultry, hot holding at 135 °F (57 °C) or higher. Cool to 70 °F (21 °C) within 2 hours and to 41 °F (5 °C) within a total of 6 hours; reheat to 165 °F (74 °C). Tenderness temperatures for brisket are a quality target, not a safety limit.
Choose a shared commissary kitchen where you can smoke: hours, storage, smoker trailer parking

cadenas.es: Furgoneta adaptada, remolque o trailer. Nuevo o 2a mano
cadenas.propuesta_en: Visit at least three and ask first: may I run a smoker here, and where does the wood go? Compare hours, walk-in space, parking for the smoker trailer and the deposit. A home kitchen is never allowed for catering, and cottage food rules do not cover meat.
Your health department asks for it with the permit application. It should name your hours, storage areas, trailer parking, smoking rules and cleaning duties; keep a signed copy on file.
Apply for the county catering / health permit and ask about the trailer

Expect an application, a fee, a menu review and an inspection of the commissary and the van. Ask your county directly: does smoking or serving from the trailer at the event make it a mobile food unit? If yes, permit it; if not, smoke at the commissary and carry the meat in hot boxes.
Check with your fire marshal on solid fuel cooking, propane and tents

cadenas.es: Planos de instalación, flujos y depósitos de agua
cadenas.propuesta_en: Cooking with wood or charcoal usually needs a Class K plus 2A:10BC extinguisher, 10 ft between your pit and other vendors and limited propane on site (often up to 200 lb). Rules follow your city's fire code, so ask the fire marshal. Check your county's burn ban order before every event (some allow cooking in a closed smoker or grill, others do not) and ask venues about cooking under tents.
Buy your smoker trailer and a used cargo van, and have both inspected

Look for an offset or reverse-flow smoker trailer in the 500-gallon class. Check welds, axles, brakes and firebox thickness, and read the title for liens. Confirm your own pickup is rated to tow it. Get a mechanical inspection of the van and check mileage, service records and payload.
Title and register the trailer and van, and buy commercial auto and inland marine coverage

Register both at your state DMV in the business name. Commercial auto should cover the trailer; inland marine covers the smoker and gear in transit. A CDL is needed only at 26,001 lb or more (pickup and trailer: a combined rating of 26,001 lb or more with a trailer over 10,000 lb). Towing across state lines above 10,000 lb combined may bring federal rules (USDOT number, DOT medical card): check with FMCSA.

Most BBQ caterers do not sell or pour alcohol: the client hires a licensed bar service with its own insurance. Skip this unless your staff pour, and ask your broker where you stand.
